rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

evidence_timeline.summary: We report multiband photometric follow-up observations of AT 2026yos (ATLAS26jvy), a rapidly fading transient discovered by ATLAS (Gillanders et al., AstroNote 2026-245). We observed the transient with the Lulin One-meter Telescope (LOT) at Lulin Observatory beginning at MJD 61264.566, approximately 1.64 days after discovery. We measure AB magnitudes of g=19.14 +/- 0.05, r=19.39 +/- 0.03, i=19.46 +/- 0.03, and z=19.53 +/- 0.09. These observations are consistent with the continuing rapid decline reported by ATLAS, while the blue colour (observed g-r = -0.26 +/- 0.06 mag) is also consistent with a possible foreground CV interpretation.

evidence_timeline.summary: Here we report the ATLAS discovery of the transient ATLAS26jvy (AT2026yos) in galaxy NGC6379 at AB magnitude, m_w = 18.53 +/- 0.04. At a distance of 87 Mpc, the transient was discovered on MJD 61262.93 (2026-08-10.93) with an absolute magnitude, M = -16.45 +/- 0.04. The last non-detection through forced photometry was on MJD 61261.97, when the transient possessed m_w > 21.4 (3-sigma). If associated with NGC6379, AT2026yos would possess a projected offset of 37.0 kpc. Further ATLAS observations indicate that AT2026yos has since faded at a rate of 0.33 mag/day. Given all of the above, we consider AT2026yos to be a plausible kilonova candidate, possessing an absolute magnitude, galaxy offset, and rise and fade rates consistent with those seen for previous events. As such, we strongly encourage spectroscopic classification.

At a distance of 87 Mpc, the transient was discovered on MJD 61262.93 (2026-08-10.93) with an absolute magnitude, M = -16.45 +/- 0.04. The last non-detection through forced photometry was on MJD 61261.97, when the transient possessed m_w > 21.4 (3-sigma). If associated with NGC6379, AT2026yos would possess a projected offset of 37.0 kpc. Further ATLAS observations indicate that AT2026yos has since faded at a rate of 0.33 mag/day. Given all of the above, we consider AT2026yos to be a plausible kilonova candidate, possessing an absolute magnitude, galaxy offset, and rise and fade rates consistent with those seen for previous events. As such, we strongly encourage spectroscopic classification.

publication_revisions.abstract: Here we report the ATLAS discovery of the transient ATLAS26jvy (AT2026yos) in galaxy NGC6379 at AB magnitude, m_w = 18.53 +/- 0.04. At a distance of 87 Mpc, the transient was discovered on MJD 61262.93 (2026-08-10.93) with an absolute magnitude, M = -16.45 +/- 0.04. The last non-detection through forced photometry was on MJD 61261.97, when the transient possessed m_w > 21.4 (3-sigma). If associated with NGC6379, AT2026yos would possess a projected offset of 37.0 kpc. Further ATLAS observations indicate that AT2026yos has since faded at a rate of 0.33 mag/day. Given all of the above, we consider AT2026yos to be a plausible kilonova candidate, possessing an absolute magnitude, galaxy offset, and rise and fade rates consistent with those seen for previous events. As such, we strongly encourage spectroscopic classification.

publication_revisions.abstract: We report multiband photometric follow-up observations of AT 2026yos (ATLAS26jvy), a rapidly fading transient discovered by ATLAS (Gillanders et al., AstroNote 2026-245). We observed the transient with the Lulin One-meter Telescope (LOT) at Lulin Observatory beginning at MJD 61264.566, approximately 1.64 days after discovery. We measure AB magnitudes of g=19.14 +/- 0.05, r=19.39 +/- 0.03, i=19.46 +/- 0.03, and z=19.53 +/- 0.09. These observations are consistent with the continuing rapid decline reported by ATLAS, while the blue colour (observed g-r = -0.26 +/- 0.06 mag) is also consistent with a possible foreground CV interpretation.
